title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
statement: You are given a linked list as a Python list `values` and a positive integer `n`. Remove the n-th node counting from the end (1-based) and return the resulting values as a Python list. `n` is always valid for the given list.
brute_force_code:
def remove_nth_from_end(values, n):
    out = list(values)
    out.pop(len(out) - n)
    return out

predict_steps.prompt: With a dummy before [1,2,3,4,5] and n=2, after fast moves n+1 steps from dummy, which value does fast sit on?
When fast reaches the end, slow sits just before the node to delete. Which node is deleted for n=2?

viva.question: Why does a lead pointer n steps ahead remove the nth-from-end in one pass?
expected_points: the fixed gap of n means follower sits before the victim when lead hits null
rewiring follower.next drops the target node
total time stays linear in the list length
a dummy head keeps the predecessor well-defined even near the front

viva.question: What breaks when n equals the length of the list?
expected_points: the node to remove is the original head
the dummy's next becomes the new head
without a dummy you would need a special case for deleting head
the lead pointer reaches null after exactly n steps from dummy

viva.question: Why does a gap of n place follower just before the victim?
expected_points: lead at null means n nodes remain after follower
the next node after follower is therefore the nth from the end
unlinking that next removes the victim
the invariant is distance(lead, follower) equals n throughout
